items.stem: Who is shown in this picture sitting on knees?
items.answer: The print is the well-known 1860 cartoon in which a man in a campaigner's shirt kneels to draw the boot marked 'ITALY' onto the foot of the crowned, robed figure of Victor Emmanuel II. The kneeling man is Giuseppe Garibaldi, who handed over the kingdom he had won in the south to the king of Sardinia-Piedmont. Hence the answer is (b) Giuseppe Garibaldi.

items.stem:
Match column A and column B and choose the correct option.
Column AColumn B
A.Absolutist1.A vision of society
B.Utopian2.A form of government
C.Plebiscite3.A system of direct vote
D.Suffrage4.A system of holding election
items.answer: Absolutism is a form of government in which power is unrestrained, so A - 2. A utopia is an imagined vision of an ideal society, so B - 1. A plebiscite is a direct vote in which the people of a region accept or reject a proposal, so C - 3. Suffrage is the right to vote, exercised through the holding of elections, so D - 4. The matching is A - 2, B - 1, C - 3, D - 4, which is (d).

items.stem: What were the consequences of the July revolution of 1830 ?

options.label: A
options.text: A constitutional monarchy with Louis Philippe at its head was installed in France

options.label: B
options.text: Uprising in Brussels took place which led to Belgium breaking away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands

items.answer: The July revolution of 1830 drove the Bourbon king Charles X from the throne and put Louis Philippe at the head of a constitutional monarchy in France. The news of it set off a rising in Brussels, and Belgium broke away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. Both consequences followed, so the answer is (c) Both a and b.

items.stem:
Identify the group of people who had -
• Commitment to oppose monarchical forms that had been established after the Vienna Congress
• Willingness to to fight for liberty and freedom.
• They saw the creation of nation-states as a necessary part of this struggle for freedom.
items.answer: After 1815 the conservative regimes restored by the Vienna Congress were autocratic, so opposition had to work in secret. The men who formed these secret societies were committed to overthrowing the monarchies, were ready to fight for liberty and freedom, and held that nation-states had to be created for that freedom to exist. Such people were called revolutionaries, so the answer is (c) Revolutionaries.
items.ocr: Second bullet is printed with a duplicated word, 'Willingness to to fight'; kept exactly as printed.

items.stem: Which among the following was the main reasons for the weavers to revolt against contractors in Silesia, in 1845?

options.label: B
options.text: They stopped the supply of the raw material to them.

options.label: C
options.text: They refuse to place orders for finished textiles.

options.label: D
options.text: It was the wave of revolution.

items.answer: The Silesian weavers worked for contractors who supplied them raw material and placed the orders for finished cloth. In 1845 those contractors cut the payment for the finished cloth drastically, and the weavers, already living in misery, marched on the contractor's mansion in protest. The cause of the revolt was therefore (a) Contractors reduced their payments drastically.
items.ocr: Stem on page 11; the four options and the key print on page 12.

items.stem: Select the name of painter in following image?
items.answer: The painting is 'The Massacre at Chios', which shows Greek villagers dying on the shore after the Ottoman reprisal of 1822. It was painted by the French Romantic artist Eugène Delacroix, and it was used to rouse European sympathy for the Greek war of independence. Hence the answer is (c) Delacroix.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements -
1. During 1789 paintings of females appeared as symbols of liberty.
2. Female figure in France was named as Marianne.
3. Germania was depicted by Kaiser William I.
4. The idea behind Marianne was to represent the French nation as people's nation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
items.answer: From 1789 artists personified liberty, justice and the republic as female figures, so statement 1 is correct. In France that figure was named Marianne, a popular Christian name that marked her as the people's nation, so statements 2 and 4 are correct. Germania is the allegory of the German nation and was painted by artists such as Philip Veit, not depicted by Kaiser William I, so statement 3 is wrong. The correct set is 1, 2 and 4, which is (c).

items.stem:
Choose the incorrect matched option from column A and B
Column AColumn B
(a)Frederic SorrieuA british artist
(b)Wolfe ToneStruggled for Ireland
(c)Lord ByronAn english poet
(d)Karol KarpinskiA polish music composer

options.label: D
options.text: Karol Karpinski - A polish music composer

items.answer: Wolfe Tone did lead the Irish struggle against British rule, Lord Byron was an English poet who died fighting for Greece, and Karol Karpinski was a Polish composer who carried nationalism into opera and music. Frederic Sorrieu, however, was a French artist, not a British one, so the wrongly matched pair is (a) Frederic Sorrieu - A british artist.

items.stem: What happened to Poland at the end of 18th century. Select the correct option?

options.label: A
options.text: Poland achieved independence at the end of the 18th century.

options.label: B
options.text: Poland came totally under the control of Russia and became part of Russia.

options.label: C
options.text: Poland became the part of East Germany.

options.label: D
options.text: Poland was partitioned at the end of the 18th century by three Great Powers: Russia, Prussia and Austria.

items.answer: Poland did not survive as a state into the nineteenth century. In a series of partitions ending in 1795 its territory was divided among Russia, Prussia and Austria, and Poland disappeared from the map, which is why Polish nationalism later grew around language, music and the Church. Hence (d) Poland was partitioned at the end of the 18th century by three Great Powers: Russia, Prussia and Austria.
items.ocr: The printed question number is covered by the vertical NODIA watermark in the gutter; it is 61 by the running sequence 60, 61, 62.

items.stem:
Identify the event-
• The first clear expression of nationalism in France.
• The transfer of sovereignty from the monarchy to a body of French citizen.
• A new French Flag, the tricolour was chosen to replace the former royal standards
• The liberation of the people of Europe from despotism.
items.answer: All four descriptions belong to one event. The French Revolution of 1789 was the first clear expression of nationalism, it shifted sovereignty from the monarchy to a body of French citizens, it replaced the royal standard with the tricolour, and the revolutionaries declared it their mission to free the peoples of Europe from despotism. Hence the event is (c) French Revolution 1789.

items.stem: Which one of the following statement is false regarding the Act of Union 1707?

options.label: A
options.text: It was an agreement between England and Scotland

options.label: B
options.text: It was an agreement between England and Ireland

options.label: C
options.text: It resulted in the formation of the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain'

options.label: D
options.text: It gave England control over Scotland

items.answer: The Act of Union of 1707 was signed between England and Scotland and created the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain', with England the dominant partner controlling Scotland's culture and institutions. Ireland was brought in only by the later Act of Union of 1801. The false statement is therefore (b) It was an agreement between England and Ireland.
items.ocr: Stem on page 12; the four options and the key print on page 13.

items.stem: Which of the following aspect best signifies this image?

options.label: C
options.text: The Frankfurt Parliament in the church of St. Paul

options.label: D
options.text: The Hall of Mirrors of Versailles

items.answer: The picture shows a large circular hall packed with elected deputies, with the black-red-gold German colours hung around the galleries and an allegory of Germania above the dais. This is the all-German National Assembly that met on 18 May 1848 in the Church of St Paul in Frankfurt. Hence the answer is (c) The Frankfurt Parliament in the church of St. Paul.

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct definition of Conservatism?

options.label: A
options.text: A direct vote by which all the people of region are asked to accept or reject a proposal.

options.label: B
options.text: A government that has no restraints on the power exercised.

options.label: C
options.text: A political philosophy that stressed the importance of tradition, established customs and institutions and preferred gradual development to quick change.

options.label: D
options.text: It was a political association who founded a women's journal.

items.answer: Option (a) defines a plebiscite and option (b) defines absolutism, while option (d) describes a women's political association. Conservatism is the political philosophy that valued tradition, established customs and institutions and accepted change only if it came gradually, which is option (c).

items.stem:
Arrange the following events of world history in increasing order of their date of occurrence
1. Unification of Italy
2. Vienna Peace Settlement
3. Napoleon wars begin
4. Unification of Germany
items.answer: The Napoleonic wars began in 1803, the Vienna Peace Settlement was signed in 1815, Italy was unified in 1861 and Germany in 1871. Placed in increasing order of date the events run 3, 2, 1, 4, which is option (a).

items.stem: Which one of the following was not implemented under the Treaty of Vienna of 1815?

options.label: B
options.text: Setting up series of states on the boundaries of France

options.label: D
options.text: Diluting the German confederation of 39 states

items.answer: The Treaty of Vienna restored the Bourbon dynasty, set up a ring of states along France's boundaries to block future expansion, and put the deposed monarchies back on their thrones. The German confederation of 39 states set up by Napoleon was left untouched, not diluted. The measure not implemented is therefore (d) Diluting the German confederation of 39 states.

items.stem: Identify the major aspect that helped in the formation of a nation-state in Britain.

options.label: A
options.text: In 1688, the monarch of Britain fought war with English Parliament.

options.label: B
options.text: The Parliament through a bloodless revolution seized power from the monarchy.

options.label: C
options.text: The British nation was formed as a result of a war with Ireland and Wales.

options.label: D
options.text: The formation of a nation-state in Britain was the result of many revolts.

items.answer: In Britain the nation-state was not built by a sudden upheaval. In 1688 Parliament took power from the monarchy through a bloodless revolution, and the English parliament then became the instrument through which Scotland and Ireland were drawn into a single British state. Hence the answer is (b) The Parliament through a bloodless revolution seized power from the monarchy.

items.stem: 'Nationalism', which emerged as a force in the late 19th century, means

options.label: A
options.text: strong devotion for one's own country and its history and culture.

options.label: B
options.text: strong devotion for one's own country without appreciation for other nations.

options.label: C
options.text: strong love for one's own country and hatred for others.

options.label: D
options.text: equally strong devotion for all the countries of the world.

items.answer: Nationalism as it emerged in the nineteenth century meant a strong attachment to one's own country together with pride in its history and culture. It did not by itself mean contempt for other nations, nor an equal devotion to every country. Hence the answer is (a) strong devotion for one's own country and its history and culture.

items.stem:
Study the picture and answer the question that follows:
Which of the following aspects best suits the 'sword' in the image?
items.answer: The picture shows the attributes given to Germania - the eagle shield, the black-red-gold flag, the crown of oak leaves, the imperial crown and the drawn sword. In this vocabulary of symbols each object carries a fixed meaning, and the sword stands for readiness to fight. Hence the answer is (c) Readiness to Fight.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements about the 'French Revolution' are correct?
(1) After the end of the French Revolution it was proclaimed that it was the people who would henceforth constitute the nation and shape its destiny.
(2) France will have a constitutional monarchy and the new republic will be headed by a member of the royal family.
(3) A centralised administrative system will be put in place to formulate uniform laws for all citizens.
(4) Imposition of internal custom duties and dues will continue to exist in France.
items.answer: The Revolution declared that sovereignty passed to the people, who would henceforth constitute the nation and shape its destiny, so statement 1 is correct, and it set up a centralised administration framing uniform laws for all citizens, so statement 3 is correct. The new republic was not headed by a member of the royal family, and internal customs duties and dues were abolished, not continued, so statements 2 and 4 are wrong. The correct pair is (1) and (3), which is (c).
items.ocr: Statements (1)-(3) print in the left column of page 14 and statement (4) with the options at the top of the right column.

items.stem:
Study the picture and answer the question that follows.
Who among the following has painted this image of Germa
items.answer: The painting shows Germania as an armoured woman with a crown of oak leaves, a drawn sword and a shield, standing guard on the Rhine. It is the 1860 canvas 'Germania on Guard on the Rhine' by Lorenz Clasen. Hence the answer is (b) Lorenz Clasen.

items.stem:
With reference to the cause of Silesian Weavers consider the following statements--
1. The cause of the silesian weavers uprising was the contractors cheating on the weavers.
2. The contractors who supplied the weavers raw materials and gave order for finished materials reduced the payments of the weavers.
Which one of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
items.answer: The Silesian weavers depended entirely on contractors who supplied the raw material and placed the orders for finished cloth. Those contractors cheated the weavers and in 1845 cut their payments drastically, which is what drove the weavers to revolt. Both statements describe the same cause correctly, so the answer is (c) Both 1 and 2.

Match the columns and choose correct option.
Column -IColumn -II
A.17971.Vienna Peace Settlement
B.18142.Invasion of Italy
C.18213.Revolution in Europe
D.18484.Struggle for Independence in Greek.
items.answer: Napoleon's armies invaded Italy in 1797, so A - 2. The Vienna Peace Settlement was drawn up by the European powers in 1814-15, so B - 1. The Greek struggle for independence began in 1821, so C - 4. The liberal revolutions swept Europe in 1848, so D - 3. The matching is A - 2, B - 1, C - 4, D - 3, which is (d).

items.stem: Which of the following is not a feature or belief of 'Conservatism'?

options.label: A
options.text: Conservatives believe in established, traditional institutions of state and policy.

options.label: B
options.text: Conservatives stressed the importance of tradition and preferred gradual development to quick change.

options.label: C
options.text: Conservatives proposed to return to the society of pre-revolutionary days and were against the ideas of modernisation to strengthen monarchy.

options.label: D
options.text: Conservatives believed in the monarchy, church, and other social hierarchies.

items.answer: The conservatives of the nineteenth century did believe in established institutions, in tradition and slow change, and in monarchy, the Church and social hierarchy. But they did not want a simple return to pre-revolutionary society; they accepted that modernisation - a modern army, an efficient bureaucracy, the abolition of feudalism - actually strengthened monarchy. The statement that is not their belief is (c).
items.ocr: Option (b) is printed with a stray soft-hyphen artefact, 'develop¬ment'; written here as 'development'.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The Balkan area became an area of intense conflict.
Reason (R) : The Balkan states were fiercely jealous of each other and each hoped to gain more territory at the expense of the others.
items.assertion: The Balkan area became an area of intense conflict.
items.reason: The Balkan states were fiercely jealous of each other and each hoped to gain more territory at the expense of the others.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: The Balkans did become a region of intense conflict in the years before 1914. The reason given explains why: the newly independent Balkan states were deeply jealous of one another and each hoped to extend its territory at its neighbours' expense, which, with the big powers competing over the same region, kept the area in turmoil. Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A, so the answer is (a).

items.stem: What was the result of the activities and campaigns held at the Jacobin clubs?

options.label: A
options.text: prepared the way for the French armies to move to different countries

options.label: B
options.text: they brought about unrest in the society

options.label: C
options.text: they brought about crime and destruction

items.answer: Students and other educated members of the middle classes set up Jacobin clubs, and the campaigns run from those clubs built support for carrying the revolution beyond France. Their activity prepared the way for the French armies that moved into Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy in the 1790s. Hence the answer is (a) prepared the way for the French armies to move to different countries.

items.stem:
Following image is the personification of Germany commonly associated with the Romantic Era and the Revolutions of 1848.
Identify its name from among the following options.
items.answer: The female figure carries the black-red-gold tricolour, wears a crown of oak leaves and bears the eagle on her breastplate - the standard attributes of the allegory of the German nation. She is Germania. Marianne is the French allegory and Philip Veit is the painter, not the figure. Hence the answer is (c) Germania.

items.stem:
Identify the personality -
• She was a political activist.
• She was an elected member of Frankfurt parliament.
• She founded a political association who was feminist in nature.
• She founded a women's journal.
items.answer: Carl Welcker was a male liberal politician of the Frankfurt parliament, Frederic Sorrieu was a French artist and Giuseppe Mazzini an Italian revolutionary, so none of them fits a woman described here. The political activist who founded a feminist political association and a women's journal in the Germany of 1848 is Otto Peter, so the answer is (a) Otto Peter.
items.ocr: The first two bullets print at the foot of page 15; the last bullets, the options and the key print on page 16.

items.stem: What did Napoleon do to make the system efficient and rational in France?

options.label: A
options.text: in the administrative field he had incorporated revolutionary principles

items.answer: Napoleon did away with the democratic republic, but he kept the gains of the Revolution in the way France was governed: the Civil Code of 1804, equality before the law, the abolition of privilege by birth and secure property rights were all carried into the administration. It was by building these revolutionary principles into the administrative field that he made the system efficient and rational, which is option (a).

items.stem:
Which of the following was a part of the Napoleonic Code?
1. The feudal system was abolished.
2. Guild restrictions were removed.
3. Weights and measures were standardised.
4. A common national currency was introduced.
items.answer: In the territories Napoleon controlled the code abolished the feudal system and freed peasants from serfdom and manorial dues, removed guild restrictions in the towns, introduced a uniform system of weights and measures and put a common national currency in place. All four measures belong to it, so the answer is (d) All the above.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements about the 'French Revolution' are correct?
1. After the end of the French Revolution it was proclaimed that it was the people who would henceforth constitute the nation and shape its destiny.
2. France will have a monarchy and will be headed by a member of the royal family.
3. A centralised administrative system will be put in place to formulate uniform laws for all citizens.
4. Imposition of internal custom duties and dues will continue to exist in France.
items.answer: The Revolution proclaimed that sovereignty had passed to the people, who would constitute the nation and shape its destiny, so statement 1 is correct, and it set up a centralised administration that framed uniform laws for all citizens, so statement 3 is correct. France became a republic rather than a monarchy headed by the royal family, and internal customs duties and dues were abolished. The correct pair is 1 and 3, which is (c).
items.ocr: Statements print in the left column at the foot of page 16 and the options with the key at the top of the right column of the same page.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : Italy was divided into seven states, of which only one was ruled by an Italian princely house.
Reason (R) : The north was under the domination of the Bourbon kings of Spain.
items.assertion: Italy was divided into seven states, of which only one was ruled by an Italian princely house.
items.reason: The north was under the domination of the Bourbon kings of Spain.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: Before unification Italy was cut into seven states, and of these only Sardinia-Piedmont was ruled by an Italian princely house, so the assertion is true. But the north was under Austrian Habsburg rule; it was the south, the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, that was held by the Bourbon kings of Spain. The reason is therefore false, and the answer is (c) A is true but R is false.

items.stem:
Which of the following is not associated with the revolt of 1848 in Paris?
1. Small producers in towns were often faced with stiff competition from imports of cheap machine-made goods from England.
2. Food shortages and widespread unemployment brought the population of Paris out on the roads.
3. National Assembly proclaimed a constitutional monarchy, granted suffrage to all adult males above 21.
4. Men and women of the liberal middle classes combined their demands for constitutionalism with national unification.
items.answer: The 1848 revolt in Paris was a revolt of the poor: small producers were being undercut by cheap machine-made imports from England, and food shortages with widespread unemployment drove the people onto the streets, so statements 1 and 2 belong to it. The National Assembly that followed proclaimed a republic, not a constitutional monarchy, and the liberal middle-class demand for constitutionalism joined to national unification belongs to the wider liberal revolution in the German lands. Statements 3 and 4 are not associated with it, so the answer is (c).

items.stem: Which of the following aspect best signifies this image of 'Germania'?
items.answer: Germania is shown wearing the crown of oak leaves, which stands for heroism, and holding the drawn sword, which in this vocabulary of symbols stands for justice and the readiness to defend it. The figure is not austere, vengeful or merely folkloric. The aspect it signifies is therefore (a) Heroism and Justice.
items.ocr: Stem on page 16; the image, the options and the key print on page 17. The printed key gives only the words 'Heroism and Justice' without an option letter; that text is option (a).

items.stem:
Which of the following is associated with the 'Revolution of the liberals 1848' ?
1. Unlike the revolt of poor in France it was led by educated middle class in Ottoman empire.
2. Men and women of the liberal middle classes combined their demands for constitutionalism with national unification
3. Demands for the creation of a nation-state on parliamentary principles – a constitution,freedom of the press and freedom of association.
items.answer: The 1848 liberal revolution was led by the educated middle classes of the German and Italian lands and the Habsburg empire, not of the Ottoman empire, so statement 1 is wrong. Men and women of those liberal middle classes did join their demand for constitutionalism to national unification, and they did press for a nation-state built on parliamentary principles with a constitution, freedom of the press and freedom of association. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is (c).

items.stem:
With reference to unification of Italy consider the following statements.
1. Cavour who led the movement to unify the regions of Italy was neither a revolutionary nor a democrat.
2. After the unification of Italy, the Habsburg rulers had more autonomy to the Hungarians
Which one of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
items.answer: Cavour, the chief minister who led the movement to unify Italy, was an aristocrat and a shrewd diplomat, neither a revolutionary nor a democrat, so statement 1 is correct. The grant of greater autonomy to the Hungarians came with the Habsburg Compromise of 1867 and had nothing to do with the unification of Italy, so statement 2 is wrong. The answer is (a) 1 only.
items.ocr: The stem and statements print at the foot of the left column of page 17 and the closing words with the options at the top of the right column.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements -
1. Balkans was a region of geographical and ethnic regions.
2. A large part of Balkans was free from the Ottomon empire.
3. The dismembering of Ottomon empire with its Balkan states became a scene of big power rivalry.
4. Balkan states were jealous of each other.
Which of the above statements are correct?
items.answer: The Balkans was indeed a region of great geographical and ethnic variety, the break-up of the Ottoman empire turned its Balkan lands into a scene of rivalry between the big European powers, and the Balkan states were fiercely jealous of one another. Statement 2 is wrong, because a large part of the Balkans was under Ottoman rule, not free of it. The correct set is 1, 3 and 4, which is (a).

items.stem:
Study the picture and answer the question that follows:
Which of the following aspect best signifies the above image?
items.answer: The picture is Delacroix's painting of a bare-breasted allegory of Liberty striding over the barricade with the tricolour raised, leading an armed crowd. The heightened emotion, the heroic figure and the appeal to feeling rather than to reason are the marks of the Romantic imagination that fed national feeling. Hence the aspect it signifies is (a) Romanticism.

items.stem:
Arrange the following events of German unification in increasing order of their date of occurrence
1 Friedrich Wilhelm IV rejected the demand of all German national assembly
2. The Frankfurt parliament convened in the Church of St Paul.
3. Kaiser William I of Prussia was proclaimed as the new German emperor.
4. Three wars over 7 years with Austria, Denmark and France was fought.
items.answer: The Frankfurt parliament met in the Church of St Paul in May 1848, so event 2 comes first. Friedrich Wilhelm IV rejected the crown offered by that assembly in 1849, so event 1 follows. Prussia then fought three wars over seven years with Denmark, Austria and France, ending in 1871, so event 4 comes next, and Kaiser William I was proclaimed German emperor at Versailles in January 1871, so event 3 is last. The order is 2, 1, 4, 3, which the book prints as option (c).
items.ocr: Option (c) is printed as '2, 1, 4, 2' and the key repeats it verbatim; the last figure is a misprint for 3, since the sequence has to end with Kaiser William I's proclamation. Key and printed answer agree, so this is a typo in the option, not a key/solution conflict. List item 1 is printed without its full stop.
